svg.title: One command = fork, exec, wait (and everything is inherited)
svg.desc: A shell command box above the six things the shell does before your program starts. To the right, the parent process forks a child, an arrow trying to send an environment change back up is crossed out in red, and the child's three inherited file descriptors show only stdout redirected to a file. Below, the nine permission bits are drawn as a three-by-three grid mapping rwxr-x--- to octal 750, and the child's exit status 1 returns to the parent as dollar-question-mark.
svg.text: One command = fork, exec, wait (and everything is inherited)
this is why cd is a builtin. A child
cannot change its parent's directory, so
an external cd would do nothing at all.
10 000 loops: 0.013 s as a builtin vs 12.863 s
an exact copy: fds, env, cwd, umask
export FOO=1 cannot flow back up
CI reads this number and nothing else
